summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with sepsis secondary to a urinary tract infection, presenting with fever, chills, and left flank pain. He has a complex urologic history including a nephroureteral stent and ileal conduit. Blood and urine cultures grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, with urine also growing E. coli. He was initially treated with gentamicin, then switched to tobramycin per infectious disease recommendations. A nephroureteral stent exchange was performed to address possible infected hardware, and a PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. His infection resolved, renal function improved to baseline, and he tolerated stent capping. He was discharged home with services to complete a 14-day course of IV tobramycin, with follow-up planned in infectious disease, nephrology, and urology.
